A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SecP-Tuning research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across reorganized sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original accuracy, runtime, communication, and deployability experiments in Tables 1–4 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports additional pretrained-prompt controls and a cosine-protocol ablation.

M1.justification: The client-side FoT/CMA-ES updates, secret-shared inference, RFA, and masked-cosine computation are retained. The Server-Client terminology and expanded explanations describe the existing workflow. Algorithm 1's corrected output label does not change its cosine-computation formula.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SST-2, Yelp Polarity, AG's News, MRPC, and RTE, with the same sequence-length and LAN/WAN scenarios. The added initialization and cosine controls introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 3 adds RFA without the proposed efficient cosine protocol as an evaluated comparator. SFT, gradient-based prompt tuning, and the FoT variant remain; the renamed FoT rows are not newly introduced methods.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds comparisons with and without pretrained prompts, and Section 5.3 describes the revised SecP-Tuning evaluation as using no pretrained prompts. The table also changes the reported AG's News metric from F1 to accuracy and MRPC from accuracy to F1, without establishing recomputation. Figure 3 adds a cosine-disabled control; the backbone, sample counts, and network settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds controls addressing both principal empirical mechanisms: Figure 3 isolates the efficient cosine protocol's contribution, while Table 2 compares pretrained and unpretrained initialization for prompt tuning and FoT on MRPC/RTE. These substantially expand the evidence separating sources of efficiency and accuracy beyond v2's existing RFA-versus-attention comparison.

E5.justification: Both versions report Table 2 means and standard deviations over three runs and Tables 1 and 4 averages over ten runs. No new seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains the earlier prompt-tuning/FoT averages of 73.73/83.14 in pretrained-prompt rows and adds unpretrained averages of 64.07/75.34. The full SecP-Tuning row averaging 82.45 is replaced by results averaging 76.58 under the revised initialization description; this is not an established same-setting performance decline. Figure 3 adds cosine-ablation results, and Table 3 changes SecP-Tuning's SST-2 accuracy from 89.2 to 89.0. LAN/WAN efficiency values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Sections 6.3.1 and 6.4.1 add elementary correctness derivations and privacy arguments for the arithmetic primitives and cosine protocol. Algorithm 1 corrects its stated output from sin(x) to cos(x) and expresses the modulus using the period tau. The RFA derivation, semi-honest assumptions, and framework-level compositional security argument remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace explicit average-performance superiority over SFT and prompt tuning with a claim of comparable performance. This substantially narrows a headline empirical claim. The first-MPC-framework positioning and central efficiency, privacy, and deployability claims are retained.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 conditions the favorable FoT interpretation on pretrained prompts while retaining the exploration-versus-overfitting explanation. Section 5.5 newly attributes RFA's practical efficiency to the cosine protocol. Section 4 also explains specific CMA-ES obstacles in MPC and discusses alternative gradient-free optimizers.

D1.justification: v2 specifies baseline Adam learning rates of 1e-5/5e-4 and training budgets of 200/1000 epochs for SFT/prompt tuning; v3 omits these details without restoring them in the appendix. Protocol walkthroughs expand, while Table 5's FoT/RFA hyperparameters, hardware, and library-access information remain.

R1.justification: Related work adds differential-privacy fine-tuning and distinguishes its privacy objective from MPC, with new foundational and application citations. PPT and Centaur are also cited, while PrivPy and AriaNN disappear. SecFormer and MPCViT publication updates represent retained works; the core MPC-versus-HE positioning remains.

P1.justification: Section 4 substantially reorganizes the threat-model, overview, FoT, and RFA narrative, incorporating the workflow into the FoT subsection and expanding explanations. The experimental discussion separates deployability and attention comparisons, and the appendices reorder protocol material and add an LLM-use disclosure. These changes extend beyond terminology or copyediting.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains grouped pretrained-prompt rows, and Figure 3 is redrawn with an additional comparator and a corrected communication-axis label. The ICLR format changes headers, typography, and float placement. Figures 1–2 and the other table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The pretrained-prompt controls and cosine ablation make the accuracy and efficiency explanations better supported, and the narrowed headline performance claim is more appropriately qualified. These gains are tempered by omitted baseline learning rates and training budgets, plus unresolved initialization documentation: Section 5.3 describes SecP-Tuning without pretrained prompts while Table 5 retains an NLI-pretrained default. The overall improvement is useful but limited.
